_doc: THE PINNED DML SURFACE OF THE DEPLOY ARTIFACT — every table, every write site, by OWNING FUNCTION.
Checked by `dml-manifest.py --manifest`, which run-tests.sh invokes on every run. Two assertions,
and the second is the one that was missing:
1. per table: the (op, owning-function) multiset matches `sites` exactly;
2. COVERAGE: the set of tables pinned here matches the set of `deftable` declarations in the
module source, so a NEW TABLE cannot arrive with an unpinned writer.
🔴 WHY IT COVERS EVERY TABLE AND NOT JUST THE FAMOUS TWO (an internal review, a finding).
Until a later change exactly two tables were pinned — `accounts` and `tallies` — and the finding that
forced this was DEMONSTRATED, not argued: a planted permissionless writer zeroing `sum-pending`
in the `state` table passed every suite and every correctness gate in the tree. `state` carries
the award solvency counters, and nothing looked at it. It was not special; 12 of the 14 tables
were in that position. Pinning the one table the finding named would have reproduced the estate's
most-repeated defect — fixing the instance and leaving the class — which is the same mistake
run-tests.sh already records at a later change ("cover the set, not the instance").
🔴 A COUNT IS NOT A MANIFEST (a later change a finding). Deleting a legitimate `(update tallies …)` and
planting one inside the PERMISSIONLESS `close-proposal` kept the count at 3 and the gate printed
"unchanged" while the mutator set had changed. Add-only and delete-only both went red; only
RELOCATION was invisible, and relocation is what an attacker-shaped edit looks like. So each site
names its owning function, and duplicate entries are meaningful (two sites in one function).
🔴 WHEN THIS GOES RED, EDITING THIS FILE IS ALMOST NEVER THE FIX. A mutator appearing, vanishing
or moving between functions is a DESIGN CHANGE. Change the code, or write the ADR, and only then
re-pin — in the same commit, saying which decision moved it.

accounts.why: the design record permits exactly ONE balance-increasing writer (`credit`, gated by CREDIT and fed by the still-pure `credit-plan`). Any other DML against `accounts` is a design change needing an ADR, not a manifest edit. `debit` legitimately holds TWO update sites.

proposals.why: Proposal records. `create-proposal` inserts; `cancel-proposal` and `close-proposal` each update twice (the row plus its active-slot bookkeeping). `close-proposal` is PERMISSIONLESS by design (the design record), so a new writer reachable from it is reachable by anyone.

account-votes.why: How many of an account's tokens are CURRENTLY voting, per proposal. Written by `cast-vote` and released by `debit` — the pairing that makes a transfer surrender the moved tokens' vote (the design record/the design record, and the fix for a defect). A third writer breaks the release invariant silently.

vote-delegates.why: the design record optional dedicated voting key. Set by `set-vote-key`, cleared by `clear-vote-key`, and auto-revoked by `rotate` — that third site is the security-relevant one: rotating the account guard must not leave a stale hot key able to vote.

tallies.why: 🔴 THE WHOLE PRODUCT RESTS ON `tallies` HAVING EXACTLY TWO MUTATORS — `cast-vote` and the release loop inlined in `debit`. `create-proposal`'s zero-row insert is a WRITER but not a MUTATOR: it cannot overwrite, because the `proposals` insert aborts first. A third mutator silently voids the product. `cast-vote` legitimately holds two update sites (the re-vote pair, remove-old then add-current; the second plan READS what the first wrote, so the order is load-bearing).

prop-index.why: The small active-proposal index the transfer release-loop iterates. Its writer is deliberately INLINED at each of the three lifecycle sites rather than factored into a helper (the project notes, the design record line) — so three write sites is the pinned shape, not a smell. Admin-created, never attacker-inflatable.

prop-count.why: Singleton counter for the active-proposal index. Seeded by both init paths (`init` on spokes, `init-supply` on chain 0) and moved by the three lifecycle functions that write `prop-index`. Its site set must track `prop-index`'s or the index and its length disagree.

state.why: 🔴 THE TABLE COLD AUDIT #14 a finding FOUND UNGUARDED, WITH A WORKING DEMONSTRATION: a planted permissionless writer zeroing `sum-pending` passed every suite and every correctness gate. `state` carries `reward-per-token`, `circulating-supply`, `rounds-applied`, `total-distributed`, `sum-pending` and `sum-debt` — the the design record exact-solvency counters, so a wrong write here does not corrupt one balance, it makes `fund-awards`'s "funded means every claim is payable" guarantee false for the whole chain. Two inserts (the two init paths) and six updates, every one on a value-moving path. the design record (a later change) adds FOUR more updaters and they are all snapshot lifecycle: `advance-snapshot` twice (the settle and the seal are separate writes), `schedule-snapshot` and `cancel-snapshot`. `advance-snapshot` is PERMISSIONLESS by design — a chain with no activity must still be sealable by anyone — so it is the one unauthenticated writer on this table and the reason the manifest names owning functions rather than counting. 🔴 the design record part 2 (a later change) adds ONE more updater, `set-runway`, and it is a different KIND from every other site here: the others move value or advance the snapshot lifecycle, this one moves a LIMIT. It is the only writer on this table gated at ADMIN-GOV (two devices) rather than ADMIN-OPS or permissionless, and that asymmetry is the safety property — if it ever appears under a one-device tier, a single key could shorten the runway and then declare inside it, reassembling the no-remedy state from two legal steps.

award-rounds.why: Declared award rounds (the design record). `declare-round` inserts; `retract-round` is the ONLY way back and works only before a round takes effect — it zeroes the rate and rewinds `effective-at` rather than deleting, because Pact has no row deletion. A new writer here is a new way to change a round's economics after declaration.

round-count.why: Singleton: how many rounds have been declared on this chain. Seeded by both init paths and advanced by `declare-round` only — note `retract-round` deliberately does NOT appear, because a retraction never rewinds the count.

tranche-locks.why: the design record time-locked reserves (cliff then linear vest). Created once by `init-supply`; moved only by the permissionless `release-tranche` and the admin `disburse-tranche`. A fourth writer is a new path to 70,000+ SPT.

init-state.why: The once-only latch. Exactly two inserts, one per init path — and INSERT is the mechanism: a second init aborts on the duplicate key rather than relying on a read-then-check. An `update` or `write` appearing here would make initialisation re-runnable.

snapshots.why: 🔴 the design record's record-date generations: `circ` is the float LATCHED at the record instant — the denominator `declare-round` enforces the rate over and the operator funds against. INSERT only in `advance-snapshot` (a generation seals exactly once; an insert on a duplicate key aborts rather than silently re-latching a float that has moved), and the `rate` field is written by exactly TWO functions: `declare-round` binds it and `retract-round` rewinds it. 🔴 BOTH SIDES OR NEITHER — the award-rounds row drives the ACCRUAL and this row drives the CORRECTION, so a rate written to one and not the other pays on the wrong denominator forever. A third writer here can re-price a sealed generation after the money was funded.

config.why: Singleton sale config (`active`, `price`). Written once by `init`, then only by the three admin operations `pause`, `resume-sale` and `set-price`. A new writer is a new way to move the price or reopen a closed sale. 🔴 the design record part 2 (a later change) adds `set-min-price`, which writes the FLOOR rather than the price. It is the only ADMIN-GOV writer on this table; `set-price`, `pause` and `resume-sale` are all ADMIN-OPS. A lowered floor followed by a lowered price is the measured reserve drain reassembled from two legal steps, which is why the two powers must not token a tier and why this row names the owner rather than counting writers.

init-state.why: The sale's once-only latch — same insert-aborts-on-duplicate mechanism as the token's. One site, one init path (the design record D1: the sale initialises on the HUB CHAIN ONLY).
